control.title: Ensure the container host has been hardened
control.description: The underlying host OS should follow an established hardening baseline; a soft host undermines every daemon-level control above it.
control.remediation: Apply a host hardening baseline (CIS OS benchmark / DISA STIG) and record attestation.

control.title: Restrict network traffic between containers on the default bridge
control.description: With inter-container communication (icc) enabled, every container on the default bridge can reach every other, so one compromise sees the rest.
control.remediation: Set "icc": false in daemon.json and define explicit networks for containers that must talk.

fix.dry_run: disable inter-container comms on default bridge; restart dockerd

results.evidence: "icc" is false; inter-container comms restricted on the default bridge

control.title: Set the logging level to 'info'
control.description: Running the daemon at debug level leaks verbose operational detail and bloats logs; 'info' is the recommended production level.
control.remediation: Remove any "log-level" override or set "log-level": "info" in daemon.json.

fix.dry_run: set daemon log level to info

control.title: Allow Docker to make changes to iptables
control.description: Disabling iptables management ("iptables": false) leaves container network isolation to hand-maintained rules that drift and fail open.
control.remediation: Do not set "iptables": false; let the daemon manage the firewall rules.

control.title: Do not use insecure registries
control.description: Insecure registries are contacted over plaintext without certificate validation, exposing images to tampering and MITM.
control.remediation: Remove all entries from "insecure-registries" and use TLS-secured registries only.

control.title: Do not use the aufs storage driver
control.description: aufs is deprecated, unmaintained, and not in the mainline kernel; it is a stability and security liability.
control.remediation: Use overlay2 (or another supported driver): set "storage-driver": "overlay2".

control.title: Configure TLS authentication for the Docker daemon socket
control.description: A daemon listening on a TCP socket without mutual TLS lets anyone who can reach the port drive Docker as root.
control.remediation: When exposing a tcp:// host, set "tlsverify": true with "tlscacert"/"tlscert"/"tlskey".

results.evidence: daemon is not exposed over TCP; TLS not required

control.title: Enable user namespace support
control.description: userns-remap maps container root to an unprivileged host UID, so a container escape does not land as host root.
control.remediation: Set "userns-remap": "default" (and provision subordinate UID/GID ranges).

control.title: Ensure authorization for Docker client commands is enabled
control.description: Without an authorization plugin, any client that reaches the daemon has full, unaudited control.
control.remediation: Deploy an authz plugin and set "authorization-plugins": ["<plugin>"] in daemon.json.

control.title: Configure centralized and remote logging
control.description: Local json-file logs are lost when a host is compromised or recycled; ship logs off-box for tamper-evident retention.
control.remediation: Set a remote "log-driver" (e.g. "syslog", "fluentd") with a "log-opts" destination.

control.title: Ensure live restore is enabled
control.description: Without live-restore, a daemon restart kills running containers, tempting operators toward risky availability workarounds.
control.remediation: Set "live-restore": true in daemon.json.

fix.dry_run: keep containers running across daemon restarts

control.title: Ensure the userland proxy is disabled
control.description: The userland proxy adds an unnecessary, occasionally-vulnerable data path; hairpin NAT via iptables is preferred.
control.remediation: Set "userland-proxy": false in daemon.json.

control.title: Ensure a daemon-wide custom seccomp profile is not disabled
control.description: Setting "seccomp-profile": "unconfined" (or equivalent) strips syscall filtering from every container by default.
control.remediation: Remove any daemon-level seccomp=unconfined; keep the built-in profile or supply a hardened one.

results.evidence: default/custom seccomp profile is not disabled daemon-wide

control.title: Ensure experimental features are not enabled in production
control.description: Experimental features are unstable and may lack security review; they should not run in production.
control.remediation: Set "experimental": false (or omit it) in daemon.json.

control.title: Ensure containers are restricted from acquiring new privileges by default
control.description: no-new-privileges blocks setuid/setgid privilege escalation inside containers; setting it daemon-wide makes it the default.
control.remediation: Set "no-new-privileges": true in daemon.json.

fix.dry_run: block privilege escalation for all containers

control.title: Ensure that the /etc/docker directory ownership is set to root:root
control.description: Non-root ownership of /etc/docker lets an unprivileged user tamper with daemon configuration.
control.remediation: chown root:root /etc/docker

control.title: Ensure that the /etc/docker directory permissions are set to 755 or more restrictive
control.description: World-writable configuration directories allow tampering with daemon settings.
control.remediation: chmod 755 /etc/docker

control.title: Ensure that the Docker socket file ownership is set to root:docker
control.description: The Docker socket is root-equivalent; incorrect ownership widens who can drive the daemon.
control.remediation: chown root:docker /var/run/docker.sock

control.title: Ensure that the Docker socket file permissions are set to 660 or more restrictive
control.description: A world-accessible Docker socket hands root-equivalent control to any local user.
control.remediation: chmod 660 /var/run/docker.sock

control.title: Ensure that the daemon.json file ownership is set to root:root
control.description: daemon.json controls the daemon's security posture; only root should own it.
control.remediation: chown root:root /etc/docker/daemon.json

control.title: Ensure that the daemon.json file permissions are set to 644 or more restrictive
control.description: Overly permissive daemon.json permissions allow unprivileged tampering with daemon settings.
control.remediation: chmod 644 /etc/docker/daemon.json

control.title: Ensure AppArmor profile is enabled
control.description: Running a container with apparmor=unconfined removes mandatory-access-control confinement.
control.remediation: Do not set --security-opt apparmor=unconfined; keep the docker-default profile or a custom one.

control.title: Ensure Linux kernel capabilities are restricted
control.description: Adding powerful capabilities (or ALL) re-arms attacks that the default capability set is meant to prevent.
control.remediation: Drop all capabilities and add back only those required (--cap-drop ALL --cap-add ...).

control.title: Ensure privileged containers are not used
control.description: A privileged container disables namespace, capability, and seccomp isolation — effectively host root.
control.remediation: Remove --privileged; grant only the specific capabilities/devices needed.

control.title: Ensure sensitive host system directories are not mounted
control.description: Mounting host paths such as / or /etc into a container exposes the host to modification and data theft.
control.remediation: Do not bind-mount sensitive host directories; if unavoidable, mount read-only and narrowly scoped.

control.title: Ensure privileged ports are not mapped within containers
control.description: Publishing a container on a host port below 1024 requires elevated privilege and widens the trust surface.
control.remediation: Map containers to non-privileged host ports (>=1024).

control.title: Ensure the host's network namespace is not shared
control.description: --network host removes network namespace isolation, letting the container sniff and bind host interfaces.
control.remediation: Do not run with --network host; use bridge or a user-defined network.

control.title: Ensure memory usage for the container is limited
control.description: An unbounded container can exhaust host memory and take down co-located workloads (DoS).
control.remediation: Set a memory limit (--memory).

control.title: Ensure the container's root filesystem is mounted read-only
control.description: A writable root filesystem lets an attacker persist tools and tamper with the running image.
control.remediation: Run with --read-only and mount tmpfs/volumes only where writes are required.

control.title: Ensure the host's process namespace is not shared
control.description: --pid host lets the container see and signal all host processes, breaking isolation.
control.remediation: Do not run with --pid host.

control.title: Ensure the host's IPC namespace is not shared
control.description: --ipc host shares System V IPC / shared memory with the host and other containers.
control.remediation: Do not run with --ipc host.

control.title: Ensure the host's UTS namespace is not shared
control.description: --uts host lets a container change the host's hostname and domain.
control.remediation: Do not run with --uts host.

control.title: Ensure the default seccomp profile is not disabled
control.description: seccomp=unconfined removes syscall filtering, exposing the full kernel attack surface.
control.remediation: Do not set --security-opt seccomp=unconfined; keep the default profile.

control.title: Ensure containers are restricted from acquiring new privileges
control.description: Without no-new-privileges, setuid binaries inside the container can escalate privilege.
control.remediation: Run with --security-opt no-new-privileges (or enable it daemon-wide).

control.title: Ensure container health is checked at runtime
control.description: Without a healthcheck, orchestrators cannot detect and recycle unhealthy containers.
control.remediation: Define a HEALTHCHECK in the image or --health-cmd at run time.

control.title: Ensure the PIDs cgroup limit is used
control.description: An unbounded PID count allows fork-bomb denial of service against the host.
control.remediation: Set --pids-limit to a sensible ceiling.

control.title: Ensure the Docker socket is not mounted inside any container
control.description: A container with the Docker socket mounted can control the daemon — a trivial host takeover path.
control.remediation: Never bind-mount /var/run/docker.sock into a container; use a scoped API proxy if needed.
